about: Measurement Health rules for scripts/health.py. One nightly red, amber, or green per store for tracking integrity, so broken numbers stay out of the brief and client reports. Grounded in Intelligence/processes/ga4-conversion-integrity.md and Kobe's findings of 2026-09-19 to 2026-09-23. Edit thresholds here, never in the script. Templates use {field} names the script fills; a field it does not know stays as written.

colors.red: The numbers named in 'blocks' are wrong tonight. They never go into the brief as fact or into any client-facing claim. Use CRM leads and state the measurement issue (SOP section 4 warning).
colors.amber: The raw total is wrong but a clean subset exists. Quote only what the detail line allows, with the caveat, never the raw total. Fix inside the week.
colors.green: No integrity rule tripped. Numbers may be quoted with their date range.
colors.grey: A core GA4 check could not run tonight (section missing or errored). Say which, never assume green.
colors.no_data: No ga4_{STORE}.json tonight. Say 'no data since {date}'.

state.days_broken: Calendar days from first_seen (or the documented known_since in open_cases, whichever is earlier) to last_seen, inclusive. A night with missing input neither advances nor clears a rule. A rule clears after clear_after_clean_nights clean evaluations in a row; cleared_on is the first clean night.

event_classes.about: Applied to GA4 event names and Google Ads conversion action names, case-insensitive, in this order: page_view, then lead, then soft. Anything else is 'other' and is never counted as a non-lead.

inputs.ga4: data/ga4_{STORE}.json from gdata.py ga4-nightly: channel_daily_last7, key_events_by_channel_last7 and _prior7, source_medium_last7 and _prior7, landing_pages_last7, target_date, errors
inputs.ga4_organic: data/ga4_organic_{STORE}.json from gdata.py ga4-nightly (written since 2026-09-23): organic_landing_last28, organic_windows
inputs.ads_meta: data/{STORE}_ads_meta.json: the Ads export 'meta' tab (last_run, per-tab status). health.py reads it itself on the shift date when it is missing.
inputs.ads_conversions: data/{STORE}_conversions_by_action_7d.txt or .json (Shaq's dump, either format) or the same tab read by health.py on the shift date
inputs.search_order: the shift's data/ folder first, then any run*/data/ folder of the same shift

NCBMW.source: Intelligence/processes/ga4-conversion-integrity.md section 5: key-event rate collapsed from about 17% to 1.3% since about 2026-09-01
NCBMW.note: If GTM history shows the 9/1 change was a deliberate un-marking of a soft event, the 17% was the inflated number: lower this baseline (or delete it) and KEY_EVENT_COLLAPSE clears.

open_cases.source: ga4-conversion-integrity.md section 5: key-event over-count, at least 2026-08-30
ga4-conversion-integrity.md section 5: key-event rate collapse, about 2026-09-01

rules.description: Store-wide key events per session. The SOP's healthy dealer range is about 2 to 6%; above 20% means a high-frequency event is marked as a key event and the number is noise. A single day above 100% catches a fresh break the same night.

severity.red: 7-day rate above red_rate_7d, or the target day above red_rate_target_day

rules.why: MCP ran 310% to 506% a day from 9/12 to 9/22 (481 key events on 149 sessions on 9/22). Every other store sits between 4% and 9% over 7 days, so 20% has wide headroom.
rules.board: Website conversions are {rate7} of visits, {k7} on {s7} ({window}); {tday} alone {kt} on {st}
rules.gm: The website records more conversions than visits, which means routine page views are being counted as leads. Do not quote its conversion number; use CRM leads until DigitalCLIQ fixes the setting.
rules.tech: GA4 Admin > Key events: un-mark every page-view style event (listed under NON_LEAD_KEY_EVENTS); keep form submit, call, chat, text. Annotate the change date and re-baseline 90 days before any month-over-month comparison (SOP section 2).

rules.description: Real lead events stopped firing. Two tests, worst wins: (1) the 7-day key-event rate against a documented baseline in 'baselines'; (2) lead-class key events per session this week against the prior week (sessions from the top-40 source/medium tables in both weeks, so the ratio compares like with like).

severity.red: rate below red_fraction_of_baseline of the baseline, or lead rate down red_drop_wow or more week over week
severity.amber: below amber_fraction_of_baseline, or down amber_drop_wow or more

rules.why: NCBMW ran 1.4% to 1.7% over 7 days on every night 9/19 to 9/23 against the SOP's 17% pre-9/1 rate. No store's clean lead-event rate is above 2% (SBMW and NOI sit near 1%), so an absolute floor would flag the healthy stores first; the collapse has to be judged against the store's own history. Largest week-over-week drop seen: NCBMW 49% on 9/19 (43 vs 90 lead events), MCP 34% on 9/21 on 21 vs 39 events.
rules.gm: The website stopped recording most of its leads. Visits look normal; the lead counter does not. Lead numbers for this store come from the CRM until the tracking is repaired.
rules.tech: Find the break date in the key-event trend, check the GTM container publish history and any template or form-vendor change on that date, then submit a test lead and watch GA4 DebugView: no event means a broken trigger, an event with no key event means the marking was lost (SOP section 3). If the drop was a deliberate un-marking, update baselines.{store} in measurement-rules.json.

rules.description: Share of 7-day key events that are page views (page_view class) or soft actions such as form starts and clicks (soft class). Classes come from 'event_classes'.

severity.red: non-lead share at or above red_share (almost nothing counted is a lead)
severity.amber: non-lead share at or above amber_share

rules.why: MCP 99% (new_VLP_visit, used_VLP_visit, new_VDP_visit and lowercase twins). SBMW 73% to 79% (schedule_service_page_view, 290 of 397 on Sep 16 to 22). NOI 72% to 80% (asc_form_engagement, a form start, 54 of 71). Amber, not red, below 90% because the submit and call events underneath check out (SBMW's matched Nick's CRM prospects on 9/22).
rules.gm: The website counts actions that are not leads ({class_plain}) as conversions, so its total runs about {inflation} the real number. Only finished forms and calls should count.
rules.tech: GA4 Admin > Key events: un-mark {non_lead_events}. Until then quote only {lead_events}, deduped for any DUPLICATE_LEAD_EVENTS pair, never the raw key-event total.

rules.description: Two different lead or unclassified key events with the same 7-day total and the same count in every channel: one submission firing two tags.

severity.amber: any matching pair at or above min_total

rules.why: SBMW form_submit and generate_lead matched channel for channel every night (29/29, 29/29, 34/34, 40/40). Below the floor and not flagged: NOI asc_form_submission = asc_form_submission_sales (6, 6, 5, 4) and MCP all_forms_pixel_web = form_submissions_all (8, 4).
rules.gm: One web form appears to be counted twice under two names, so form leads look double what they are.
rules.tech: {pairs}: same total and same count in every channel over {window}, one submit firing two tags. In GTM find the second tag on the same trigger; keep one as the key event and un-mark the other.

rules.description: Landing page rows (7 days, top 40 by sessions) where key events reach or pass sessions at a 100% engagement rate (a key event fires on page load, and a key event marks the session engaged), or pass twice the sessions (multi-fire). When the store's key events are mostly non-lead, the page view already flagged by NON_LEAD_KEY_EVENTS explains the shape, so this rule stays clean with a note and re-checks the page once that is fixed.

severity.red: flagged rows carry red_share_of_key_events or more of the store's key events

rules.why: ATLAS /contact: 192 generate_lead on 167 sessions at exactly 100% engagement (Sep 16 to 22), 73% of the store's key events, while every other ATLAS page converts in single digits. generate_lead is ATLAS's only key event, so there is no clean subset. SBMW's /service/schedule-service/ (72 on 33) and MCP's home page (1,327 on 305) show the same shape but are explained by their page-view key events, so they are not double counted here.
rules.board: {page} records a lead on page load, {ke} on {sessions} visits ({window})
rules.gm: A page on the site records a lead the moment someone opens it, before they fill anything in, so the site's lead count is mostly page visits.
rules.tech: Key events at or above sessions at 100% engagement on {page} means the trigger is page load or page view, not form success. Move the trigger to the form's success event or thank-you page, confirm in DebugView, annotate the date (SOP sections 2 and 3).

rules.description: Share of 28-day Organic Search sessions (AI engines excluded) whose landing page is '(not set)'.

severity.amber: share at or above amber_share with at least min_sessions

rules.why: NCBMW 403 of 2,137 organic sessions (18.9%, 28 days to 9/22). The other four stores run 3.5% to 7.4%.
rules.board: {share} of Google organic visits have no landing page, {notset} of {total} ({window})
rules.gm: A large share of Google organic visits arrive without the landing page recorded, so page-by-page SEO reporting is incomplete. Totals are fine.
rules.tech: '(not set)' landing means the session's first hit was not a page_view: a late Google tag, consent mode, events after a session timeout, or server-side hits. Check the GA4 config tag fires first (Initialization trigger) on every template in GTM preview.

rules.description: Organic Search sessions (28 days) carrying a paid-looking campaign name ('paid_campaign' pattern), Google Business Profile campaigns excluded ('gbp_campaign' pattern).

severity.amber: at least min_sessions and min_share of organic sessions

blocks: GA4 organic vs paid channel split
rules.why: NCBMW constellation_2026_bmwwr_vla (lowercase; the uppercase twin is tagged google / cpc) put 553 sessions, 26% of organic, into Organic Search over 28 days to 9/22. MCP's 'listings' and 'gbp' are Business Profile and correctly excluded.
rules.board: Paid campaign counted as organic: {campaigns}, {sessions} visits, {share} of organic ({window})
rules.gm: Visits from a paid Google campaign are being counted as free Google traffic, so organic looks bigger and paid looks smaller than they really are.
rules.tech: {campaigns} land in Organic Search: its tracking template sets a utm_medium other than cpc or overrides auto-tagging. Fix the final URL suffix (utm_medium=cpc) or rely on gclid; Worthy excludes these sessions from organic reads until then.

rules.description: Share of Google Ads primary conversions (metrics_conversions, 7 days) from actions that are not leads by 'event_classes' (store visits count as leads).

severity.red: non-lead share at or above red_share

rules.why: ATLAS counts one action, 'About Us' page views (9 on 9/19, 33 on 9/22), 100%. MCP runs 21% to 31% non-lead (map directions) and NOI 0%, both under the amber line.
rules.board: Google Ads counts {top_action} as its conversion, {share} of {total} ({window})
rules.gm: Google Ads is being told a page view is a conversion, so it reports and optimizes toward page visits, not leads. Ads conversion numbers for this store are not leads.
rules.tech: Google Ads > Goals > Conversions: set {non_lead_actions} to Secondary and make a real lead action Primary (calls from ads, form submit import). Resolve anything marked Misconfigured or Needs attention first (SOP section 4).

rules.description: Hours between the Ads export's meta last_run and the moment the meta tab was read, plus any export tab whose status is not ok.

sections: meta tab: last_run, tab status rows

severity.amber: older than amber_hours, or a tab status not ok

rules.why: data-sources.md: a last_run older than 26 hours means the export is stale. The meta tab was never saved to a shift folder before this script, so the back-test cannot check it.
rules.board: Google Ads export last ran {last_run}, {age_h} hours before it was read{tab_note}
rules.gm: Last night's Google Ads numbers did not refresh, so any Ads figure for this store tonight is from an older day.
rules.tech: Open the ads_export.gs script in the account (Tools > Scripts), check run history and authorization, run it once by hand, then re-run health.py.

rules.description: The GA4 file's target_date is older than the day before the shift, or the file lists pull errors.

severity.amber: lag above max_lag_days, or any error in the file

blocks: GA4 numbers dated as last night
rules.why: Law 2: missing or old data is reported, never carried forward as current.
rules.board: GA4 file is stale or partial: {finding}
rules.gm: Tonight's website numbers are not from last night, so they may be out of date.
rules.tech: Re-run gdata.py ga4-nightly for the shift's target date and check its errors list: {finding}.
